validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed by 5+ independent origins — (1) Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Planned Projects' trade listing (rev 6/18): 'Buncombe County Pipeline Enhancement Project', 12 miles, 12-inch, Arden NC-Enka NC, Start 2Q2019/Completion 4Q2019, upgrading the Buncombe County system to DOT compliance; (2) National Park Service Draft EA + FONSI (signed 2022-11-18 by Regional Director Mark Foust) authorizing a horizontal-directional-drill crossing of the Blue Ridge Parkway at MP 393.3, Buncombe County NC, for Dominion Energy North Carolina's 12-inch pipeline; (3) Asheville Citizen Times, 2022-12-01: '11 miles Dominion Energy has already built of 12-inch diameter steel natural gas pipeline, which starts at Duke Energy's Asheville Energy Plant in Arden and currently ends near the intersection of U.S. 23 and N.C. 112 in Enka Village'; (4) WLOS (ABC13 Asheville) coverage of the same FONSI; (5) WSET (Lynchburg VA ABC affiliate) coverage naming the same 760-ft final HDD segment completing 'a larger 10-mile, 12-inch diameter natural gas line'; (6) S&ME (project geotechnical/environmental engineer) case study on 'Dominion Energy T-072 Natural Gas Pipeline', ~11.1 miles / 12-inch steel, connecting Duke Energy's Asheville Combined Cycle Station, 11 HDDs incl. 3 French Broad River crossings + 1 I-26 crossing — hand-confirmed as this same pipeline: url_verifier's literal-name check FAILs on smeinc.com because the page calls the project by its internal designation 'T-072' rather than 'Buncombe County Pipeline', but the crossing count, river/interstate crossings, Duke Asheville plant terminus, mileage and diameter are identical to the FONSI/Citizen-Times description of this exact project (the FONSI/oilandgaswatch title also refers to it as 'DENC T2'), so this is the same line under an internal project number, not a different pipeline. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas pipeline (Fuel=Gas confirmed everywhere); worth noting for context (not a sheet field in this worklist) that the NPS EA describes the enhancement as repurposing part of the corridor 'from transmission service to lower pressure distribution service' — a scope note, not a misclassification. DUPLICATE: checked against all 41 rows in the roster; no overlap — the only other North Carolina row is P0355 (T-030 Pipeline, Franklinton-Clayton NC, unrelated corridor 150+ miles away; see cross_row_leads). ROUTE: the routes-repo geometry (P0311.geojson, single LineString, 6 points) runs from about (-82.659, 35.545) near Enka to about (-82.540, 35.472) near Arden/the Duke Energy Asheville plant — i.e. digitized end-to-start relative to the sheet's Arden->Enka convention, which is a direction artifact, not a mismatch (per the routes-vs-sheet rule); the corridor plausibly matches the Arden-Enka path described in the sources. No route concern filed.

Enbridge Inc. announced (2024-10-01/10-02 press releases) it had completed acquisition of Public Service Company of North Carolina, Incorporated (PSNC — the utility that owns/operates this pipeline, formerly a SCANA subsidiary, then a Dominion Energy subsidiary since Jan 2019) from Dominion Energy; PSNC now does business as Enbridge Gas North Carolina. Independent corroboration beyond Enbridge's own release: (a) World Pipelines trade-journal coverage of the same close; (b) structural evidence — dominionenergy.com's North Carolina gas project pages (including this project's own former page, en-espanol variant) now 302-redirect to enbridgegas.com/north-carolina, and PSNC's own former project page (psncenergy.com/about-us/service-area-map/buncombe-county-pipeline-enhancement-project) and its 'Study Corridor / SCANA T027' PDF (wiki citations #2 and #5) have both been replaced by generic Enbridge marketing pages with no Buncombe-specific content — i.e. the operator itself confirms the transition by no longer hosting the old material. status_reviews.researcher_notes: No source dated after mid-2023 explicitly states the pipeline is now in service — that is the honest limit of this finding — but the convergent circumstantial case is strong: (1) NPS signed the FONSI for the last remaining segment 2022-11-18; (2) Dominion's own Nov/Dec 2022 statement (reported independently by both the Asheville Citizen Times and WSET) targeted construction Q1 2023 and completion Q2 2023 for that final ~760-ft HDD crossing, with 11 of ~12 miles already built by that point; (3) S&ME's case study touts the project (as 'T-072') winning the 2022 ACEC/NC Engineering Excellence Grand Conceptor award, consistent with a substantially-finished project; (4) as of this 2026-09 review, Enbridge Gas North Carolina's current public 'Projects' listing (enbridgegas.com/about-enbridge-gas/projects) shows only newer active NC projects (e.g. T15 Reliability Project, Chatham County System Expansion) and no Buncombe/T-072 entry, consistent with it no longer being an open project; (5) over three years have elapsed past the Q2 2023 target with no press coverage of further delay, cancellation, or safety incident found. I searched specifically for post-2023 confirmation (Asheville Citizen Times, Asheville Watchdog, Mountain Xpress, EIA pipeline-projects workbooks, NCUC docket search) and could not find one — NCUC's docket-detail pages return HTTP 403 to automated fetch, which is the main gap; a human search of starw1.ncuc.gov or the Buncombe/Dominion 'T-072' CPCN docket directly would likely close it. Given the weight of the schedule + elapsed-time + absent-from-current-projects-list evidence, I am proposing the change to 'operating' at tier=medium (not high, since no single source states the fact directly) rather than leaving this 'stale' — the dormancy rules are a poor fit for a project that was already ~92% physically built and fully permitted for its last segment, as opposed to a project with no construction activity.
